Beneath the symptom in Workforce Scheduling & Field Orchestration sits the same defect everywhere: judgment work trapped inside manual assembly. The composition below is the way out.

We build demand-aware orchestration: forecasting into shift and route planning, skills/certs-aware assignment, agentic exception handling (absences, overruns), and compliance evidence produced automatically.

blocks.x: Workforce Scheduling & Field Orchestration composes Dataq Swarm, Dataq Nexus — platforms with documented controls and evidence packs, so governance is part of the runtime. The pattern is in delivery now in Telecom, Media & Entertainment, Logistics & Supply Chain, Energy & Utilities, Retail & Consumer Goods.

The Workforce Scheduling & Field Orchestration engagement opens with the problem stated in the CFO's units and a baseline signed by whoever owns the number. Design follows with the risk envelope explicit; the proof phase runs a bounded slice on your data with falsifiable gate criteria; industrialization scales only what the evidence supports. What we promise is modest and checkable: a signed baseline, a bounded slice in production, and evidence your auditors can read without a guide. For Workforce Scheduling & Field Orchestration, that discipline is not optional — it is the engagement model.
